source.title: A Description of the Cards of the Tarot with their Attributions; including a Method of Divination by their use
source.work: Book T, the Golden Dawn tarot document, as printed in The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 8
source.edition: The Equinox, Vol. I, No. 8 (London, 1912), pp. 143–210; scan of the printed pages. Public domain.
source.note: Read from the page images, not from OCR. Astrological glyphs are written out as words; `printed` keeps them as set. Hebrew letter names are the usual transliterations of the printed letters. The Equinox renames Book T's court figures: its Knight is Book T's King on horseback and its King is Book T's Prince in a chariot (footnote p. 159), and its Knave is the Princess ("The Four Princesses are the Knaves of the Tarot Pack", p. 157); ids follow the RWS names used in content/kb (11 Page, 12 Knight, 13 Queen, 14 King). This is the 1912 printing, not the Golden Dawn manuscript. Details: docs/research/kb-source-verification-2026-10.md
